nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a move relation on a type of positions, where $R\,x\,y$ means that $y$ is an option of $x$, and suppose that there is no infinite sequence of moves (the relation "$y$ is an option of $x$" is well-founded). If $P$ and $Q$ are both sets of P-positions for $R$, then $P = Q$.

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and consider Slow$\{k\}$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks, in which a move removes one token from each of exactly $k$ nonempty stacks. For every position $x \in \mathbb{N}^{k+1}$, the basic-vector value $B(x)$ equals Smith's remoteness of $x$ in this game.

Let $j$ be a pile with $x_i > 0$ for every $i \ne j$, and let $x'$ be obtained from $x$ by removing one token from every pile other than $j$. Then $B(x') \le B(x) - 1$ and $B(x')$ is odd. Moreover, if $z_j < B(x)$,…
nodes.title: Moves at a position supported by an (A0) basic vector (Lemma 2)

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $B$ be the basic-vector value on $\mathbb{N}^{k+1}$, and let $x, z \in \mathbb{N}^{k+1}$ with $z \le x$ componentwise, where $z$ is a basic vector of type (A1) with parameter $B(x)$. Then every option $x'$ of $x$ in Slow$\{k\}$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks (a move removes one token from each of exactly $k$ nonempty stacks) satisfies $B(x') \ge B(x) - 2$, and the position $x''$ obtained from $x$ by the…
nodes.title: Moves at a position supported by an (A1) basic vector (Lemma 3)

Then $x = z$, and every option $x'$ of $x$ in Slow$\{k\}$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks (a move removes one token from each of exactly $k$ nonempty stacks) satisfies $B(x') = B(x) - 1$, where subtraction is truncated at $0$.

nodes.summary: The bitstring encoding of $\mathbb{N}$ that writes $0$ as the empty string and a positive integer $n$ as its binary digits, least significant bit first, together with Mathlib's decoding map, which recovers $n$ from its encoding. It is a definition, not an instance; Theorem 3 installs it locally so that lists of piles are encoded as self-delimiting binary blocks.
nodes.title: Binary encoding of natural numbers

Then the entries of $x$ are either all odd or all even. If they are all even, then some entry satisfies $x_i < m$; every option $y$ of $x$ with $y_i < x_i$ for every $i$ such that $x_i = m$ is $(m - 1)$-critical; and the position $x'$ obtained from $x$ by the M-move satisfies…
nodes.title: Moves from critical positions with even parameter (Corollary 1 (i))

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$, let $m$ be odd, and let $x \in \mathbb{N}^{k+1}$ be an $m$-critical position of Slow$\{k\}$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks. Then $x$ has exactly one even entry $x_i$. The position $x'$ obtained from $x$ by removing one token from every pile other than $i$ is an option of $x$, it is the only option of $x$ that is $(m - 1)$-critical, and it is the position reached from $x$ by the M-move.
nodes.title: Unique critical-lowering move for odd parameter (Corollary 1 (ii))

nodes.summary: For a position $x \in \mathbb{N}^{n+1}$ with piles indexed by $0, \dots, n$: if some entry of $x$ is even, the kept pile is the least index $i$ such that $x_i$ is even and $x_i \le x_j$ for every $j$ with $x_j$ even; otherwise it is the least index $i$ such that $x_j \le x_i$ for every $j$.
nodes.title: Pile kept by the M-rule

nodes.summary: Let $k, f \in \mathbb{N}$ and $x \in \mathbb{N}^{k+1}$, and write $M_f(x)$ for the number of M-rule steps from $x$ in Slow$\{k\}$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks, counted for at most $f$ steps. Then $M_{f+1}(x) = 0$ if $x$ has no options, and otherwise $M_{f+1}(x) = 1 + M_f(x')$, where $x'$ is the position obtained from $x$ by the M-move.
nodes.title: Successor step of the truncated M-rule length

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $f$ be natural numbers and let $x$ be a position on $k + 1$ piles. Call $x$ terminal when $k = 0$ or fewer than $k$ of its piles are nonempty. The value at $f$ and $x$ is $0$ when $f = 0$ or $x$ is terminal; otherwise it is $1$ plus the value at $f - 1$ and the position reached from $x$ by the M-move. Thus it counts the M-moves played from $x$, stopping at a terminal position or after $f$ moves.
nodes.title: Fuel-bounded length of M-rule play

nodes.summary: Let $0 < k$ and let $\mathrm{NIM}(k + 1, k)$ be exact slow $k$-NIM on $k + 1$ piles, that is, Slow$A$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks with $A = \{k\}$, where a move removes one stone from each of exactly $k$ nonempty piles. For every position $x$ of $\mathrm{NIM}(k + 1, k)$, the M-rule length $M(x)$ equals Smith's remoteness $R(x)$ of $x$ in $\mathrm{NIM}(k + 1, k)$.
nodes.title: Theorem 2 (the M-rule realizes Smith's remoteness)

nodes.summary: In exact slow $2$-NIM on three piles, $\mathrm{NIM}(3, 2)$, where a move removes one stone from each of exactly two nonempty piles, the M-rule length of the position $(3, 5, 5)$ is $M(3, 5, 5) = 6$.
nodes.title: M-rule length of the position (3, 5, 5)

nodes.summary: In exact slow $2$-NIM on three piles, $\mathrm{NIM}(3, 2)$, where a move removes one stone from each of exactly two nonempty piles, the M-rule length of the position $(3, 3, 3)$ is $M(3, 3, 3) = 4$.
nodes.title: M-rule length of the position (3, 3, 3)

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_k)$ be a position on $k + 1$ piles. Then $M(x)$ is the number of M-moves played from $x$ until a terminal position (one with $k = 0$ or fewer than $k$ nonempty piles) is reached, computed as the fuel-bounded length of M-rule play with fuel $x_0 + \dots + x_k$.
nodes.title: M-rule length

nodes.summary: For a position $x$ on $n + 1$ piles, the M-move keeps one pile, chosen by the M-rule as the first pile holding the smallest even entry if some entry of $x$ is even, and otherwise the first pile holding a largest entry. It removes one stone from every other pile, where an empty pile stays empty.
nodes.title: The M-move

nodes.summary: Let $0 < k$ and let $\mathrm{NIM}(k + 1, k)$ be Slow$A$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks with $A = \{k\}$. A position $x = (x_0, \dots, x_k)$ of $\mathrm{NIM}(k + 1, k)$ all of whose entries are odd is a P-position if and only if there is a natural number $m$ such that $x_0 + \dots + x_k = km + k - 1$, $x_i < m$ for every $i$, and $m$ is even.
nodes.title: Proposition 1 (odd P-positions of exact slow k-NIM)

Here natural numbers, in the input and the output, are encoded in binary, and a list is encoded as the concatenation of the self-delimiting forms of the encodings of its…

nodes.summary: For a list $(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ of natural numbers of length $n$, the value is Smith's remoteness of the position $(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks with $A = \{n - 1\}$, where $0 - 1 = 0$. For $n = k + 1$ this game is exact slow $k$-NIM $\mathrm{NIM}(k + 1, k)$, so $k$ is part of the input; the empty list gives the game on no stacks.
nodes.title: Remoteness of exact slow k-NIM from a list of piles

nodes.title: The basic value is attained

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $b$ be natural numbers. A vector $z = (z_0, \dots, z_k)$ of $k + 1$ natural numbers is basic of type (A0) for $b$ when $z_0 + \dots + z_k = kb$, $z_i \le b$ for every $i$, $b$ is even, and every $z_i$ is even.

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $b$ be natural numbers. A vector $z = (z_0, \dots, z_k)$ of $k + 1$ natural numbers is basic of type (A1) for $b$ when $z_0 + \dots + z_k = kb$, $z_i \le b$ for every $i$, $b$ is odd, and exactly one $z_i$ is even.

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $b$ be natural numbers. Here $kb + k - 1$ is computed in the natural numbers, so it is $0$ when $k = 0$.

nodes.title: Set of P-positions

nodes.summary: For every $n$ and every finite set $A$ of natural numbers, the position of Slow$A$-Nim $\mathrm{SN}(n, A)$ with all $n$ stacks empty has no move to any position in the playable game graph of $\mathrm{SN}(n, A)$.

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a position of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks, with $p_i$ tokens on stack $i$, and let $S$ be a set of stacks. The position after playing on $S$ is obtained by removing one token from each stack of $S$: its stack $i$ holds $p_i - 1$ if $i \in S$ and $p_i$ otherwise, where an empty stack of $S$ stays empty.

nodes.title: The empty position is a P-position

nodes.summary: For every finite set $A$ of natural numbers and every position $p$ of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks, the empty sequence of moves is legal from $p$.
nodes.title: The empty move sequence is legal

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of natural numbers and $p$ a position of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks. A finite sequence $S_1, \dots, S_m$ of sets of stacks is legal from $p$ when it is empty, or when $S_1$ is nonempty, $|S_1| \in A$, every stack in $S_1$ holds at least one token in $p$, and $S_2, \dots, S_m$ is legal from the position obtained from $p$ by removing one token from each stack of $S_1$.
nodes.title: Legal move sequences in Slow A-Nim

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers and let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be a position of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ piles with $A = \{k\}$. Then $x$ has no options if and only if $k = 0$ or fewer than $k$ of the piles are nonempty.
nodes.title: Terminal positions of exact slow $k$-NIM

nodes.summary: For every finite set $A$ of natural numbers, the position of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks in which every stack is empty has no options.
nodes.title: The empty position has no options

The options of $p$ in Slow$A$-Nim are the positions obtained from $p$ by choosing a nonempty set $S$ of stacks with $|S| \in A$, each holding at least one token, and removing one token from each stack of $S$.

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ be even and let $A = \{1, n\}$. A position $p = (p_1, \dots, p_n)$ of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks is a P-position if and only if its total number of tokens $p_1 + \dots + p_n$ and its smallest stack $\min_i p_i$ are both even.
nodes.title: P-positions of Slow A-Nim with A = {1, n}, n even

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be odd with $1 \le k \le n$ and let $A = \{1, k\}$. A position $p = (p_1, \dots, p_n)$ of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks is a P-position if and only if its total number of tokens $p_1 + \dots + p_n$ is even.
nodes.title: P-positions of Slow A-Nim with A = {1, k}, k odd

nodes.summary: Let $A = \{1, 2\}$ and let $p = (p_1, \dots, p_5)$ be a position of Slow$A$-Nim on five stacks in canonical form, that is, $p_1 \le p_2 \le \dots \le p_5$. Then $p$ is a P-position if and only if all five stacks are even, or $p_1, p_2$ are even and $p_3, p_4, p_5$ are odd, or $p_1, p_2, p_5$ are odd and $p_3, p_4$ are even, or $p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4$ are odd and $p_5$ is even.

nodes.title: P-positions of Slow $\{1,2\}$-Nim on four stacks

nodes.summary: In Slow $A$-Nim with $A = \{1, 2\}$ on three stacks, let $p = (p_0, p_1, p_2)$ be a position with $p_0 \le p_1 \le p_2$. Then $p$ is a P-position if and only if its three stack heights are all even or all odd.
nodes.title: P-positions of Slow $\{1,2\}$-Nim on three stacks

nodes.title: The reduction never adds tokens

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of natural numbers and let $p$ be a position of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks. For each stack $i$, let $u_i(p)$ be the least height of stack $i$ over all terminal positions (positions with no moves) reachable from $p$ by a sequence of zero or more moves. The reduction of $p$ is the position $r(p)$ with $r(p)_i = p_i - u_i(p)$ for every stack $i$.
